3D Hover Options

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/3d-hover.Rmd
3d-hover.Rmd

Customize Hover for Spikelines

By default, Plotly’s 3D plots display lines called “spikelines” while hovering over a point. These lines project from the hover point to each of the three axes’ normal planes and then extend from those projection data points to the planes’ wall boundaries.

library(plotly.core)

mtcars$am[which(mtcars$am == 0)] <- "Automatic"
mtcars$am[which(mtcars$am == 1)] <- "Manual"
mtcars$am <- as.factor(mtcars$am)

am_colors <- c(Automatic = "#BF382A", Manual = "#0C4B8E")

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = am_colors) |>
  add_scatter3d(
    x = ~wt,
    y = ~hp,
    z = ~qsec,
    mode = "markers",
    opacity = 0.8,
    marker = go_scatter3d_marker(color = ~am)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    scene = go_scene(
      xaxis = go_scene_axis(
        spikecolor = "#a009b5",
        spikesides = FALSE,
        spikethickness = 6
      ),
      yaxis = go_scene_axis(
        spikecolor = "#a009b5",
        spikesides = FALSE,
        spikethickness = 6
      ),
      zaxis = go_scene_axis(
        spikecolor = "#a009b5",
        spikethickness = 6
      )
    )
  )

Customize Hover for Surface Contours

In addition to spikelines, Plotly 3D Surface plots also display surface contours on hover by default. These are customized by styling the contours attribute in the surface trace (see go_surface_contours()).

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_surface(
    z = ~volcano,
    contours = go_surface_contours(
      x = go_surface_contours_axis(highlight = TRUE, highlightcolor = "#41a7b3"),
      y = go_surface_contours_axis(highlight = FALSE),
      z = go_surface_contours_axis(highlight = FALSE)
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    scene = go_scene(
      xaxis = go_scene_axis(showspikes = FALSE),
      yaxis = go_scene_axis(showspikes = FALSE),
      zaxis = go_scene_axis(showspikes = FALSE)
    )
  )

Reference

See go_scene_axis() and go_surface_contours() for more information and options!
